newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended mixed on Wednesday, but an enormous asset swap deal by broker SBC Warburg boosted turnover into record territory, dealers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said.

The asset swap, which dealers said probably represented a portfolio being moved offshore, lifted overall trading value to 2.776 billion rands worth of shares -- beating the previous April 29 record of 2.171 billion rand.
A Warburg spokesman confirmed the trades had taken place involving most major blue-chip shares, but declined to give further details.
Dealers at other brokerages said Warburg's deal had covered about two billion rands worth of the day's trade.

Major volumes surrounded Barlows, up 15 cents at 48.00 rand in trade worth 155 million rand, Sasol, off 100 cents to 55.50 rand in trade worth 127 million rand, Johnnic, up 50 cents to 57.75 rand in trade worth 98 million rand, Liberty, up 100 cents to 123.25 rand in trade worth 81 million rand, and DiData up 10 cents to 16.30 rand in trade worth 79 million rand.
The huge volumes in major shares provided a firm tone for the market, which had been expected to head downwards, bullied by futures traders rushing to settle positions ahead of Friday's close-out.

The all-share index ended up 26.3 points to 7,218.4 as industrials dropped just 0.6 points to 8,432.1. Futures activity in the market was seen as light with some spot selling in the morning and some buying in the afternoon.
But the underlying sentiment in the market is being hit by concerns over a weakening bond market and a shakey currency ahead of the relaxation of exchange controls on July 1.
"Today was a unique day due to the Warburg asset swap. Underneath it people are a little nervous," one dealer said.
Dealers expected futures players to start taking a more active role in the rest of the week with only two days before their near-dated contracts close-out.
"We should should start moving down to the end of the week, but not by that much," one dealer said.

Futures traders said their market had opened weaker, but then picked up as the day wore on. The all-share June contract was last at 6,447/58 from 6,388 with the industrials contract at 7,967/72 from 7,946.

Among individual shares Gencor added 165 cents to end at 20.75 rand after news of a spin-off of its Billiton base metals operation to list in London and plans to raise more than $1 billion overseas. The firm also sealed a nickel merger deal with Australia's QNI Ltd.
"Gencor looks very good. We are impressed with the whole deal," said James Scott, equity marketing manager at SocGen Frankel Pollak.
Diamond gaint De Beers added 50 cents to 166.00 rand after first half diamond sales figures came in up 4.81 percent to $2.880 billion.

In smaller stocks, both Toco Holdings and Gallagher came off recent lows. Toco, which has been hit by several profit warnings, added three cents to 38 cents and Gallagher, hammered on Tuesday after poor results, clawed back five cents to 104 cents.
The gold market was stranded by little real interest. The share index ended down 3.8 points at 1,096.7 as the futures contract was last at 770/774 from 764.
"There was a little interest in gold futures, but not much else," said one dealer.
Dealers said shares were suffering from a bleak outlook on the prospects for the bullion price that emerged from a recent gold conference in Prague.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
